notes: Derived edit. Planet types are individuals (instance_of). The definitional premise 'a moon orbits a planet of a given type exactly when the planet it orbits is of that type' is a SWRL rule one way (orbits_planet_of_type is functional, so it can't be a chain target) and a class axiom per type the other way, so the premise route reaches an unnamed planet. The direct question ('a terrestrial planet or a gas giant?') presupposes the two types exclude each other (firm disjointness). q1's original 'no' needs a terrestrial planet not to be mostly hydrogen and helium (the record's 'Mars's rocky make-up goes with its type'): make-up is one-valued per type. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30 (mostly_made_of is built_from). built_from is many-valued in the catalogue; the question takes one value for granted, so Func(built_from) is a firm background fact here (built_from_one_value).

type_rule: orbits_planet_of_type value gas_giant ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value gas_giant)
orbits_planet_of_type value terrestrial ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value terrestrial)
make_up: instance_of value gas_giant ⊑ built_from value h_he
instance_of value terrestrial ⊑ built_from value rock_metal
